<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Press release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Rio Tinto delivers record underlying earnings of $14&nbsp;billion and announces $5&nbsp;billion
capital management programme together with 20 per cent increase in dividend</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>10 February&nbsp;2011</B>

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Record underlying earnings<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">1</SUP> of $14.0&nbsp;billion, 122 per cent above 2009.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Record underlying EBITDA<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">1</SUP> of $26.0&nbsp;billion, 82 per cent above 2009.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Record cash flows from operations, up 70 per cent to $23.5&nbsp;billion.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Net debt reduced to $4.3&nbsp;billion at 31 December&nbsp;2010, from $18.9&nbsp;billion at 31 December
2009.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Final dividend of 63 US cents per share increases total dividends for 2010 to 108 US
cents per share, up 20 per cent compared with previous commitment of 90 US cents per
share.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Capital management programme announced, comprising a $5&nbsp;billion share buyback by the end
of 2012.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>$12&nbsp;billion of major capital approvals since the start of 2010.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Chairman&#146;s comments</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Chairman Jan du Plessis said &#147;This year&#146;s record results reflect a combination of strong
commodity markets, first class assets and excellent operational performance at our managed
operations.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;We are in a significant growth phase and have multiple opportunities to pursue. Our strategy
remains the same, and our strengthened balance sheet means we are in a good position to
deliver on this. We will continue to make substantial investments in value-adding organic
growth and targeted small to medium-sized acquisitions.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;Our confidence in the quality of our tier one assets and our positive view of future commodity
demand growth have allowed us to increase the annual dividend by 20 per cent compared with our
previous commitment, setting a baseline for a progressive dividend policy. We continue to be
committed to efficient capital management. We also believe that the creation of shareholder
value over the long term requires a balanced approach to investing in growth and returning
excess capital to shareholders whilst maintaining a strong balance sheet. That is why we are
proceeding with a $5&nbsp;billion share buy-back programme which, subject to market conditions, we
intend to complete by the end of 2012. This significant commitment still leaves us with the
flexibility to take advantage of future growth opportunities as and when they arise.&#148;
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Chief executive&#146;s comments</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Chief executive Tom Albanese said &#147;Rio Tinto is reinvigorated, running strongly and
benefiting from favourable markets. GDP growth in emerging markets and supply constraints mean
the general market and pricing outlook for commodities remain positive, albeit with elevated
risk. In particular, the timing and speed at which post-global financial crisis stimulus
packages are removed have the potential to generate both volatility and substantial swings in
commodity prices. We are well placed to cope with the risks of both short term volatility and
long term demand growth.
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&#147;In 2010, by safely running many of our operations at full capacity we more than doubled our
underlying earnings to $14&nbsp;billion. Our leadership in operational performance was demonstrated
by record iron ore production from our world class Pilbara operations.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&#147;Our strong balance sheet, high quality assets and positive long term outlook enable us to
undertake our largest ever growth programme at the same time as returning capital to
shareholders.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&#147;Our priority remains to invest in value-adding growth. We will continue to expand our tier
one assets following the $12&nbsp;billion of major capital project approvals since the start of
2010. We have embarked on Australia&#146;s largest fully integrated mining project through the
expansion of our iron ore business in the Pilbara towards 283&nbsp;million tonnes a year by 2013,
and continue to finalise studies into the phase two expansion to 333&nbsp;million tonnes a year by
2015. We have a range of other value-adding options for growth across our diverse portfolio
including the modernisation and expansion of our aluminium smelters in Canada.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&#147;We now manage the Oyu Tolgoi copper/gold project in Mongolia following a new agreement with
Ivanhoe and have agreed a pathway to increase our stake in Ivanhoe to 49 per cent.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;On 23 December&nbsp;2010, we announced a recommended A$16 per share cash offer for Riversdale
Mining, which now has the unanimous support of Riversdale&#146;s Board. Today the offer has been
extended to 4 March.
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&#147;Our long-established strategy of focusing on long-life, cost competitive, expandable assets,
together with our increased investment in technology, positions us advantageously to enhance
shareholder value over the longer term.&#148;</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Commentary on the Group financial results</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">2010 underlying earnings of $13,987&nbsp;million and net earnings of $14,324&nbsp;million were
$7,689&nbsp;million above and $9,452&nbsp;million above the comparable measures for 2009. The principal
factors explaining the movements are set out in the table below.

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">
<DIV align="center">

<!-- End Table Body -->

</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Prices</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The effect of price movements on all major commodities in 2010 was to increase underlying
earnings by $9,505&nbsp;million compared with 2009. Prices improved for nearly all of Rio Tinto&#146;s
major commodities: copper prices were up 47 per cent, molybdenum prices were up 45 per cent,
gold prices were up 26 per cent and aluminium prices were 31 per cent higher than 2009. Demand
and prices for diamonds and minerals improved significantly as the worldwide economy emerged
from the global financial recession.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">During 2010, iron ore pricing moved to quarterly contracts, reflecting the structural shift
away from annual benchmark pricing. First quarter iron ore prices (from 1 January&nbsp;2011) are
based on the average indexed price from 1 September to 30 November&nbsp;2010.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">2010 saw continuing strength in the seaborne market for Australian coal. Demand for thermal
coal continued to be robust from South Korea, India, Taiwan and China. Global steel demand
improved in all markets throughout the year and led to strong demand for semi-soft coking
coal. The market for premium quality hard coking coal remained steady in 2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exchange rates</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">There was significant movement in the US dollar in 2010 relative to the currencies in
which Rio Tinto incurs the majority of its costs. Compared with 2009, on average, the US
dollar weakened by 16 per cent against the Australian dollar and by ten per cent against the
Canadian dollar. The effect of all currency movements was to decrease underlying earnings
relative to 2009 by $1,171&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Volumes</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Higher sales volumes were primarily generated from the expanded iron ore operations in the
Pilbara region of Western Australia running at above nameplate capacity and an increased
proportion of higher margin pellet sales at IOC. The Aluminium group benefited from higher
sales of value added aluminium products. Increased volumes of hard coking coal following new
investment in heavy mobile equipment at the Queensland mines, higher refined gold and
molybdenum at Kennecott Utah Copper and a significant recovery in diamonds and minerals market
demand also contributed to the positive variance. These increases offset lower copper and gold
volumes at Grasberg which was impacted by lower ore grades and lower mill throughput. The
overall impact of volume movements was an increase in underlying earnings of $782&nbsp;million
relative to 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Energy, other cash costs and exploration</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Higher energy costs across the Group, in particular for Aluminium, reduced underlying
earnings by $232&nbsp;million. This primarily reflected low snow and rain levels in the Saguenay
region of Quebec during the first half of 2010 which led to reduced power generation, resulting
in the need to purchase additional power under a specially negotiated power block from the
state utility over a 12&nbsp;month period.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Higher other cash costs during 2010 decreased underlying earnings by $445&nbsp;million compared with
2009. Higher unit cash costs in the Copper group were the result of the planned smelter shutdown
and lower copper production following lower grades at most of the operations. Adverse weather
conditions and higher stripping rates impacted costs at the Energy group. These were partly
offset by lower costs in the Aluminium group, which benefited from lower prices for caustic,
pitch and coke.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2010, evaluation work accelerated at many of the Group&#146;s projects including the Resolution
and La Granja copper projects and the Simandou iron ore project. Two undeveloped coal
properties were divested in 2010 resulting in a $229&nbsp;million gain on disposal, compared with a
gain of $797&nbsp;million in 2009 from the disposal of two undeveloped potash properties. The
impact from higher exploration and evaluation expenditure combined with lower gains realised
from divestments was to lower underlying earnings by $690&nbsp;million compared with 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Interest/tax/other</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The effective corporate income tax rate on underlying earnings, excluding equity accounted
units, was 27.9 per cent compared with 24.8 per cent in 2009. The increase largely related to
the one-off non-taxable profit on disposal of the potash assets which was recognised in 2009.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>




<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">



<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10618u1061800.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">

</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The group interest charge was $110&nbsp;million lower than in 2009, mainly reflecting lower debt in
2010 following completion of the rights issues and divestments.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Items excluded from underlying earnings</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto consolidated Oyu Tolgoi LLC on 15 December&nbsp;2010 following the signing of a new
agreement with Ivanhoe Mines. The $531&nbsp;million gain arising on consolidation represents the
excess of the provisional fair value ascribed to the Group&#146;s indirect share of the assets and
liabilities of Oyu Tolgoi LLC over the historic cost of acquiring that share through its
investment in Ivanhoe Mines.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Profits on the disposal of businesses in 2010 relate primarily to the sale of the Group&#146;s
remaining 48 per cent interest in Cloud Peak Energy Inc. In 2009, the Group completed the
divestments of its interests in the Ningxia aluminium smelter, the Corumb&#225; iron ore operation,
the Jacobs Ranch coal mine, Alcan Composites and 52 per cent of the Group&#146;s interest in Cloud
Peak Energy Inc.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The 2010 impairment charge of $836&nbsp;million related mainly to the Alcan Engineered Products
businesses. On 5 August&nbsp;2010, the Group received a binding offer for the sale of 61 per cent
of Alcan Engineered Products to certain investment funds affiliated with Apollo Global
Management, LLC (Apollo) and the Fonds Strat&#233;gique d&#146;Investissement. The divestment was
completed on 4 January&nbsp;2011.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2009, the Group recognised an impairment charge of $1.6&nbsp;billion with respect to Alcan
Engineered Products, Alcan Packaging and the Group&#146;s aluminium and diamond businesses. In
addition, the Group paid a break fee of $195&nbsp;million ($182&nbsp;million post-tax) to Chinalco and
incurred post-tax restructuring and severance costs of $231&nbsp;million. All of these items were
excluded from underlying earnings.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Cash flow</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Cash flows from operations, including dividends from equity accounted units, was
$23.5&nbsp;billion, 70 per cent higher than 2009, primarily as a consequence of higher prices.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Purchase of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets was $4.6&nbsp;billion in 2010, a
decrease of $0.8&nbsp;billion from 2009. This included the Brockman 4 iron ore mine development in
Western Australia, the expansion of the Yarwun alumina refinery, the commissioning of the
Clermont thermal coal mine and the extension and expansion of the Kestrel coking coal mine.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Dividends paid in 2010 of $1.8&nbsp;billion compared with $0.9&nbsp;billion in 2009 reflected
the suspension of the 2009 interim dividend.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Statement of financial position</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Net debt decreased to $4.3&nbsp;billion from $18.9&nbsp;billion at 31 December&nbsp;2009 following the
receipt of proceeds from the divestment programme and strong operating cash flows. Net debt to
total capital was six per cent at 31 December&nbsp;2010 and interest cover was 27 times.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto consolidated Oyu Tolgoi LLC on 15 December&nbsp;2010 following the signing of a new
agreement with Ivanhoe Mines. 100 per cent of Oyu Tolgoi LLC&#146;s identifiable assets and
liabilities have been recognised in the statement of financial position at fair values estimated
with the assistance of an independent third party valuer, together with goodwill. The historic
cost of acquiring the Group&#146;s indirect share of Oyu Tolgoi LLC through its investment in Ivanhoe
Mines was deducted from Investments in equity accounted units. The Group&#146;s remaining interest in
the assets of Ivanhoe that does not relate to Oyu Tolgoi LLC continues to be equity accounted.
The transaction generated a non cash gain of $531&nbsp;million.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Due to the complexity of the valuation process, and the proximity of the date on which the
agreement was signed to the reporting date, fair values on consolidation are provisional and
will be subject to further review during the 12&nbsp;months from the date on which the agreement
was effective.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Profit for the year</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2010, profit for the year was $15,184&nbsp;million (2009 $5,335&nbsp;million) of which $860
million (2009 $463&nbsp;million) was attributable to non-controlling interests, leaving $14,324
million (2009 $4,872&nbsp;million) of net earnings attributable to Rio Tinto shareholders. Net
earnings and underlying earnings, which are the focus of the commentary in this report, deal
with amounts attributable to equity shareholders of Rio Tinto.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Dividends</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Dividends are determined in US dollars. Rio Tinto plc dividends are declared and paid
in pounds sterling and Rio Tinto Limited dividends are declared and paid in Australian
dollars, converted at exchange rates applicable on 8 February&nbsp;2011.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On announcing the $15.2&nbsp;billion rights issues on 5 June&nbsp;2009, the Group stated that the total
cash dividend for the 2010 financial year would be at least equal to the total cash dividend
payment for 2008 of $1.75&nbsp;billion, equivalent to US 90 cents per share. In August&nbsp;2010, the
Group declared an interim dividend of US 45 cents per share which was paid in September&nbsp;2010.
The final dividend of US 63 cents per share increases total dividends for 2010 to 108 US cents
per share, 20 per cent higher than the previous commitment of 90 US cents per share. The total
dividend for 2010 of US 108 cents per share will form the basis of a progressive dividend
policy. The aim of Rio Tinto&#146;s progressive dividend policy is to increase the US dollar value
of ordinary dividends over time.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">From 2011, the Group will continue with its previous dividend practice of paying an interim
dividend that is half the prior year&#146;s full year dividend. Therefore, the 2011 interim
dividend is expected to be US 54 cents.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto Limited shareholders will be paid dividends which will be fully franked. The board
expects Rio Tinto Limited to be in a position to pay fully franked dividends for the
foreseeable future.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The respective dividends will be paid on 31 March&nbsp;2011 to holders of ordinary shares and ADRs.
This will apply to Rio Tinto plc and ADR shareholders on the register at the close of business
on 4 March&nbsp;2011 and to Rio Tinto Limited shareholders on the register at the close of
business on 8 March&nbsp;2011. The ex-dividend date for Rio Tinto plc, Rio Tinto Limited and Rio
Tinto ADR shareholders will be 2 March&nbsp;2011.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto plc shareholders may elect to receive their dividend in Australian dollars, and
Rio Tinto Limited shareholders may elect to receive their dividend in pounds sterling.
Currency conversions will be determined by reference to the exchange rates applicable to
pounds sterling and Australian dollars five days prior to the dividend payment date.
Currency elections must be registered by 9 March&nbsp;2011 for Rio Tinto Limited shareholders and
by 10 March&nbsp;2011 for Rio Tinto plc shareholders.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Following the consolidation of Oyu Tolgoi LLC, capital expenditure for 2011 is expected to be
approximately $13&nbsp;billion. This includes $2.3&nbsp;billion for the Oyu Tolgoi project (approved and
funded by Ivanhoe). It also includes $4.5&nbsp;billion for sustaining capital expenditure (Rio
Tinto funded).
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Evaluation expenditure in 2011, including the Simandou iron ore project and the Resolution
and La Granja copper projects, is expected to be around $900&nbsp;million.

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Notes to financial information by business unit</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Business units have been classified according to the Group&#146;s management structure.
Generally, business units are allocated to product groups based on their primary product. The
Energy group includes both coal and uranium businesses. The Diamonds &#038; Minerals product group
includes businesses with products such as borates, talc and titanium dioxide feedstock together
with diamonds operations. The Copper group includes certain gold operations in addition to
copper. The Aluminium group excludes Alcan Engineered Products which is included in &#145;Other
Operations&#146; and Alcan Packaging which is included in &#145;Net assets held for sale&#146;.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Aluminium is now presented based on commercial activities splitting it between Bauxite and
Alumina, Primary Metal and Other product group items. 2009 comparative information has been
restated accordingly.
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(a)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Gross sales revenue includes 100 per cent of subsidiaries&#146; sales revenue and the
Group&#146;s share of the sales revenue of equity accounted units (after adjusting for sales to
subsidiaries).</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(b)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>EBITDA of subsidiaries and the Group&#146;s share of EBITDA relating to equity accounted
units represents profit before: tax, net finance items, depreciation
and amortisation. Underlying EBITDA excludes the same items that are excluded from Underlying
earnings.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(c)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Net earnings represent profit after tax for the year attributable to the owners of the
Rio Tinto Group. Earnings of subsidiaries and equity accounted units are stated before
finance items but after the amortisation of discount related to provisions. Earnings
attributed to business units do not include amounts that are excluded in arriving at
Underlying earnings</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">

per cent).</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>

</TR>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Notes to financial information by business unit (continued)</B>
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(m)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Capital expenditure comprises the net cash outflow on purchases less disposals of
property, plant and equipment, capitalised evaluation costs and purchases less disposals
of other intangible assets. The details provided include 100 per cent of subsidiaries&#146;
capital expenditure and Rio Tinto&#146;s share of the capital expenditure of equity accounted
units. Amounts relating to equity accounted units not specifically funded by Rio Tinto
are deducted before arriving at total capital expenditure for the Group.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(n)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Operating assets of subsidiaries comprise net assets excluding post retirement assets
and liabilities, net of tax, and are before deducting net debt. Operating assets are less
non-controlling interests, which are calculated by reference to the net assets of the
relevant companies (i.e. net of such companies&#146; debt).</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(o)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Includes Rio Tinto&#146;s interests in Oyu Tolgoi LLC which are held indirectly through
its investment in Ivanhoe and were recognised at a provisional fair value on 15 December
2010. The Group&#146;s remaining interest in the assets of Ivanhoe Mines that does not relate
to Oyu Tolgoi LLC continues to be recognised at historic cost.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>

    <TD width="3%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(p)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Net assets held for sale at 31 December&nbsp;2010 relate to Alcan Engineered Products
(AEP)&nbsp;excluding the Cable Division; at 31 December&nbsp;2009 these comprised Alcan Packaging
and other assets held for sale. In 2009, AEP was included within Other Operations.</TD>
</TR>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Performance</I></B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Iron Ore group&#146;s underlying earnings of $10,189&nbsp;million in 2010 were 147 per cent higher
than 2009, mainly reflecting higher prices due to improved market conditions, the move to
quarterly pricing from 1 April and strong production and sales volumes. Volumes increased
following the completed capacity expansion to 220&nbsp;million tonnes per annum in the Pilbara.
Capital expenditure was lower in 2010 following the completion of the Mesa A and Brockman 4
mines in the Pilbara on schedule and below budget.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Markets</I></B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Sales volumes from the Pilbara region of Western Australia continued to set new records in
response to growing demand. Full year volumes increased nine per cent to 223&nbsp;million tonnes (100
per cent basis). Shipments to major markets increased as economic conditions improved earlier
than expected, and there were delays in new capacity from other suppliers.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Operations</I></B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Pilbara operations set a new annual production record at 224&nbsp;million tonnes (100 per cent
basis) as the mines operated near or above nameplate capacity throughout the year, with
improved capability from the integrated system following the commissioning of the Operations
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>



<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always">&nbsp;</H5><P>
<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10618u1061800.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">
<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->

    <TD width="50%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="5%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="45%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<TR></TR>

    <TD valign="top"><DIV style="margin-left:0px; text-indent:-0px">Continues

<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Centre in Perth. The new wholly owned Hamersley mines, Brockman 4 and Western Turner
Syncline, continued to ramp up whilst Robe River benefited from rising production at Mesa A.
In October Robe River reached a new milestone with the export of its one billionth tonne of
iron ore.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>New projects and growth</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">During the fourth quarter, Rio Tinto announced investments of $4.3&nbsp;billion (Rio Tinto share
$3.3&nbsp;billion) towards the progressive Pilbara expansions to 283&nbsp;million tonnes per annum.
Total Pilbara investment approvals in 2010 were $7.2&nbsp;billion (Rio Tinto share $5.3&nbsp;billion).
</div>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">
On 8 February&nbsp;2011, Rio Tinto approved $933&nbsp;million for the second phase of the Marandoo mine
extension project. First ore is scheduled for 2014.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s integrated iron ore operations in the Pilbara are being progressively upgraded as
follows:
</DIV>

February&nbsp;2011, Rio Tinto announced the approval of $277&nbsp;million (Rio Tinto share $163
million) for the further expansion of IOC capacity to 23.3&nbsp;million tonnes per annum by 2013.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2010, Rio Tinto advanced to the next stage of developing its world-class Simandou iron ore
project in Guinea, approving $170&nbsp;million of further funding. Rio Tinto is engaged in an
ongoing discussion with the new Government of Guinea, in order to establish a clear pathway for
development.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Performance</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Aluminium group&#146;s underlying earnings of $773&nbsp;million were $1,333&nbsp;million improved over the
loss recorded in 2009. This was principally as a result of higher exchange traded aluminium
prices. The overall impact of price was to increase earnings by $1,569&nbsp;million
compared with 2009. This was partly offset by adverse currency movements of $391&nbsp;million,
mainly from the strengthening of the Canadian and Australian dollars against the US dollar.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always">&nbsp;</H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">



<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10618u1061800.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">
<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="55%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="5%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="45%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<TR></TR>
<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->

    <TD valign="top"><DIV style="margin-left:0px; text-indent:-0px">Continues
</DIV></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top">Page 17 of 44</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The improvement in earnings was also attributable to higher sales of value-added aluminium
products and cost savings from lower input prices for caustic, coke and pitch in the first part
of the year, partly offset by inflation and higher energy costs.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Markets</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The 2010 spot aluminium price averaged $2,173 per tonne, an increase of 31 per cent on
2009.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The aluminium market benefited from higher premiums in 2010, reflecting the combination of a
robust recovery in end-use demand in developed economies and the continued roll-over of
inventory financing positions amidst a prolonged period of low interest rates.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Operations</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Bauxite production was nine per cent higher for the full year in line with rising third
party demand. Alumina production increased three per cent on 2009 when production cutbacks
were made, primarily at the Vaudreuil refinery.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Full year aluminium production was in line with 2009. Kitimat output was reduced due to the
closures of lines 7 and 8 in September in preparation for the modernisation project. Laterri&#232;re
returned to full production at the end of September following a power outage in July which
forced the temporary closure of one of the plant&#146;s two potlines. The loss of metal production
during the partial shutdown was around 24,000 tonnes. Other movements included higher
production at NZAS following a transformer failure in 2008, which impacted 2009, and a gradual
return to full capacity at the operating UK smelters, partly offset by the cessation of
smelting activities at Anglesey.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Low snow and rain levels in the Saguenay region of Quebec during the first half of 2010 led to
reduced power generation, resulting in the need to purchase additional power under a specially
negotiated power block from the state utility over a 12&nbsp;month period. The impact on EBITDA in
2010 was approximately $117&nbsp;million.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto Alcan has implemented a metal sales hedging strategy to protect the downside risk of
three higher cost smelters, representing approximately eight per cent of forecast production in
2011.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>New projects and growth</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 23 September, Rio Tinto Alcan announced a $347&nbsp;million project to increase the annual
production capacity at its aluminium smelter in Straumsvik, Iceland (ISAL), following the
completion of a long-term energy supply agreement. This modernisation project is expected to
boost production capacity from 190,000 tonnes to 230,000 tonnes. On 1 October, a further $140
million investment was announced in a leading-edge casting facility to produce value-added
billet at ISAL.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 14 December, Rio Tinto announced that it is to invest in its Canadian aluminium smelters to
improve production efficiency through modernisation and expansion. An initial investment of
$758&nbsp;million will be spent on completing the first phase of the AP60 plant in
Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean, Quebec. An additional $300&nbsp;million will be invested for further
construction in preparation for the anticipated $2.5&nbsp;billion modernisation of the Kitimat
smelter in British Columbia.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Performance</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Copper group&#146;s underlying earnings of $2,534&nbsp;million were 35 per cent higher than 2009,
mainly reflecting higher prices. This benefit was partly offset by lower volumes, notably from
Grasberg and higher unit cash costs in line with reduced production from lower grades.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Markets</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Copper group benefited from higher average prices for its major products in 2010. Copper
increased 47 per cent to 340 cents per pound, gold increased 26 per cent to $1,222 per ounce and
molybdenum increased 45 per cent to $16 per pound.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The total impact of price changes on the Copper product group, including the effects of
provisional pricing movements, was to increase underlying earnings by $1,399&nbsp;million
compared with 2009.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">At the end of 2010, the Group had an estimated 270&nbsp;million pounds of copper sales that were
provisionally priced at US 428 cents per pound. The final price of these sales will be
determined during the first half of 2011. This compared with 267&nbsp;million pounds of open
shipments at 31 December&nbsp;2009, provisionally priced at US 335 cents per pound.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Operations</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">At Kennecott Utah Copper, lower ore grades accounted for much of the decrease in the annual
production of copper, gold and silver in concentrates. This was partly offset by record mill
rates at the Copperton concentrator. Molybdenum production rebounded in the full year in line
with an increase in ore grades
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">At Escondida, increased ore hardness and lower shovel availability at the mine led to further
decreases in copper concentrate production. At Grasberg, Rio Tinto&#146;s share of joint venture
copper and gold was impacted by lower ore grades and lower mill throughput.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>New projects and growth</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Construction of the $469&nbsp;million Eagle nickel and copper mine and mill began in 2010 with first
production expected in late 2013. The mine will produce separate nickel and copper concentrates
containing an anticipated average of 17,300 and 13,200 tonnes per year of nickel and copper
metal respectively over six years.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Construction of the Kennecott Utah Copper Molybdenum Autoclave Process (MAP)&nbsp;facility
restarted in 2010, with the investment of $340&nbsp;million in phases one and two of the
project.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 15 December, Rio Tinto assumed management of the Oyu Tolgoi project under a new agreement
with Ivanhoe Mines. Rio Tinto increased its interest in Ivanhoe to 40.5 per cent and committed
to fully participate in Ivanhoe&#146;s rights offering. Following the closing of the rights offering
in February&nbsp;2011, Rio Tinto increased its interest in Ivanhoe to 42.1 per cent through
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10618u1061800.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">the previously announced acquisition of an additional ten million Ivanhoe shares from Citibank
plus an anti-dilution adjustment for the rights offering. Rio Tinto also secured the right to
increase its ownership in Ivanhoe to 49 per cent.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Prior to Rio Tinto becoming the development and operating manager of Oyu Tolgoi, Ivanhoe&#146;s
Board of Directors and the Oyu Tolgoi Technical Committee approved a capital estimate of $4.5
billion from 2011 to 2013 to complete the 100,000 tonnes of ore per day first phase of the
project. This brings the total estimated capital cost for phase one to $5.9&nbsp;billion.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Energy</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 16pt; width: 18%; border-top: 1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

    <TD width="3%"></TD>
    <TD width="1%"></TD>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">1</SUP> </TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><I>EBITDA and underlying earnings in 2010 included $435&nbsp;million pre-tax and $229
million post-tax gain from the sale of two undeveloped coal projects.</I></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>



<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Performance</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Energy group&#146;s underlying earnings of $1,187&nbsp;million, which were two per cent higher than
2009, were impacted by adverse exchange rate movements from a stronger Australian dollar versus
the US dollar. This was offset by higher realised prices and the divestment of two undeveloped
coal projects in Australia. The $435&nbsp;million pre-tax and $229&nbsp;million post tax and minorities
gain on disposal has been recognised within underlying earnings within Energy evaluation
projects.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Markets</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Average coal prices were lower than in 2009 due to the absence of higher carry over prices
from 2008 that were reflected in the first quarter of 2009.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">2010 saw continuing strength in the seaborne market for Australian coal. Demand for thermal
coal continued from South Korea, India, Taiwan and China. Global steel demand improved in all
markets in the first half of the year and led to strong demand for semi-soft coking coal. The
market for premium quality hard coking coal remained steady in 2010.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Uranium spot markets were relatively weak early in 2010 but strengthened in the second half of
the year, mainly driven by strong demand from China. Long term prices have remained consistent
with some small increases in the later part of the year. The long term demand outlook remains
positive as many countries including China continue to expand their domestic nuclear industry.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Operations</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Hard coking coal production from the Queensland coal operations increased by 20 per cent,
benefiting from the recent investment in two additional shovels and two new truck fleets and
strong operational performance from Kestrel underground mine. The current severe wet season
which has already caused major flooding, and is predicted to continue to produce higher than
average rainfalls, had a slight impact on 2010 production levels and will continue to impact
production rates in the first quarter of 2011.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>



<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always">&nbsp;</H5><P>
<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10618u1061800.gif" alt="(RIO TINNTO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">
<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->

    <TD width="47%"></TD>

<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Semi-soft coal production was seven per cent higher than the prior year, primarily due to coal
seam presentation in the mining sequence relative to comparable periods. Production from the
Australian thermal coal operations declined by nine per cent compared with 2009, mainly due to
Blair Athol winding down while Clermont ramps up production and wet weather in the Hunter
Valley.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Uranium production declined 20 per cent year on year. This mainly reflected lower output at ERA
which was impacted by prolonged wet weather which limited access to the Ranger pit resulting in
lower average feed grade. Production was also adversely affected by mine sequencing issues
associated with the area of instability on the south wall of the pit.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 28 January&nbsp;2011, ERA announced a temporary suspension of the processing plant for 12&nbsp;weeks to
help ensure that levels in the Tailings Storage Facility remain below the authorised operating
limit throughout the remainder of the wet season.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>New projects and growth</I></B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Clermont thermal coal mine in Queensland commenced production in 2010 with full capacity
expected to be reached in 2013. It will largely replace the Blair Athol mine as it winds down
to 3&nbsp;million tonnes per annum.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The extension and expansion of the Kestrel coking coal mine in Queensland to an anticipated 5.7
million tonnes per annum is expected to come onstream in late 2012 / early 2013.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Diamonds &#038; Minerals</B>

<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 16pt; width: 18%; border-top: 1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top:3pt"><div style="margin-left: 22px; text-indent: -22px"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><I>1</I></SUP>
<I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; EBITDA and underlying earnings in 2009 included $818&nbsp;million pre-tax and $797
million post-tax gain from the sale of the undeveloped potash assets in Argentina and Canada.</I>
</DIV></DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Performance</I></B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Diamonds &#038; Minerals group&#146;s underlying earnings of $328&nbsp;million were 59 per cent lower
than 2009, when a $797&nbsp;million gain was recognised from the sale of potash projects in
Argentina and Canada. Excluding this gain, Diamonds &#038; Minerals underlying earnings increased
by $325&nbsp;million due to a recovery in volumes and prices from improved market conditions and
tax benefits largely associated with a one-off charitable donation of land.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Markets</I></B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Sustained demand from emerging markets, which largely offset the slower recovery from the
established markets of the US and Europe was reflected in higher prices and increased sales
volumes for the Diamonds &#038; Minerals group.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rough diamond prices demonstrated a robust recovery throughout 2010 as demand from emerging
markets, notably India and China, accelerated. In the short run, the sustainability of this
recovery will be, in part, dependent on US consumer confidence.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>



<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio --><!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always">&nbsp;</H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">



<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10618u1061800.gif" alt="(RIO TINNTO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">
<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->

    <TD align="right" valign="top">Page 21 of 44</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Demand for titanium dioxide feedstocks, talc and borates in 2010 continued to demonstrate a
healthy recovery in line with improving global economic conditions.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Operations</I></B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Diamond production of 13.8&nbsp;million carats returned to normal levels of activity following
the shutdowns in 2009. Argyle ore grades were lower as the mine transitioned from open pit
to underground.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Higher titanium dioxide feedstock production reflected improved market conditions and included
increased QMM ore from the Madagascar mine processed in Quebec, partly offset by the reduced
shareholding in RBM following the BBBEE transaction in December&nbsp;2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Minerals production in 2010 continued to demonstrate a healthy recovery in line with improving
global economic conditions: borate production improved by 18 per cent and talc production was
up 13 per cent compared with 2009. Borate production declined at the end of December due to
abnormally high rainfall.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>New projects and growth</I></B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Diavik underground mine produced its first ore in March&nbsp;2010. The Argyle underground
project was restarted in 2010 following the approval of the remaining $803&nbsp;million in
September&nbsp;2010. The Argyle underground mine is expected to be fully operational in 2013 with
targeted production of 20&nbsp;million carats a year. It is designed to extend the mine life to at
least 2019. Prefeasibility studies began at Bunder, a diamond project in India.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Other Operations</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s US Coal business has been moved to Other Operations, following the completion
of the divestment of Rio Tinto&#146;s remaining 48 per cent stake in Cloud Peak Energy Inc on 20
December&nbsp;2010. Rio Tinto has retained its 100 per cent interest in Colowyo.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Trading conditions in the Alcan Engineered Products businesses improved during 2010. On 4
January&nbsp;2011, Rio Tinto completed the divestment of 61 per cent of Alcan Engineered Products to
certain investment funds affiliated with Apollo Global Management, LLC (Apollo) and the Fonds
Strat&#233;gique d&#146;Investissement.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Central Exploration and Evaluation</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="64%">&nbsp;</TD>

<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Central exploration expenditure in 2010 (post disposals and post tax) resulted in a charge to
underlying earnings of $52&nbsp;million compared with a credit of $5&nbsp;million in 2009, as the result
of an increased spend on greenfield exploration and lower divestments of central exploration
properties. During 2010 the Group realised $59&nbsp;million (post tax) from the divestment of these
properties compared with $76&nbsp;million in 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">A non-binding Memorandum of Understanding was signed with Chinalco on 3 December&nbsp;2010 to
establish an exploration joint venture (JV)&nbsp;in China. The JV will explore mainland China for
world-class mineral deposits and is expected to come into operation in the first half of 2011.
It is intended that between three and five large area exploration projects will be selected for
initial focus by the JV, with the potential for additional regions to be added at a later date.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">At the Amargosa bauxite project in Brazil, the Order of Magnitude study continued and remains on
track for completion in the fourth quarter of 2011.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Price &#038; exchange rate sensitivities</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The following sensitivities give the estimated effect on underlying earnings assuming that
each individual price or exchange rate moved in isolation. The relationship between currencies
and commodity prices is a complex one and movements in exchange rates can cause movements in
commodity prices and vice versa. The exchange rate sensitivities quoted below include the effect
on operating costs of movements in exchange rates but exclude the effect of the revaluation of
foreign currency working capital. They should therefore be used with care.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining Rio Tinto
plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on the Australian
Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products are
aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals (borax,
titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are strongly
represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South America, Asia,
Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>

Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. All statements other than statements of historical
facts included in this announcement, including, without limitation, those regarding Rio Tinto&#146;s
financial position, business strategy, plans and objectives of management for future operations
(including development plans and objectives relating to Rio Tinto&#146;s products, production
forecasts and reserve and resource positions), are forward-looking statements.

which may cause the actual results, performance or achievements of Rio Tinto, or industry

expressed or implied by such forward-looking statements. Such forward-looking statements are
based on numerous assumptions regarding Rio Tinto&#146;s present and future business strategies and
the environment in which Rio Tinto will operate in the future. Among the important factors that
could cause Rio Tinto&#146;s actual results, performance or achievements to differ materially from
those in the forward-looking statements include, among others, levels of actual production
during any period, levels of demand and market prices, the ability to produce and transport

recent Annual Report and Accounts in Australia and the United Kingdom and the most recent Annual

latest financial statements, which are in the process of being audited. This announcement does not
constitute the full financial statements, which are to be approved by the Board and subsequently
filed with the Australian Securities &#038; Investments Commission.

Corporations Act 2001 issued by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission on 22 December
2010.

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(a)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Gross sales revenue includes the sales revenue of equity accounted units (after adjusting
for sales to subsidiaries) of US$4,254&nbsp;million (31 December&nbsp;2009: US$3,197&nbsp;million) in
addition to Consolidated sales revenue. Consolidated sales revenue includes subsidiary sales
to equity accounted units, which are not included in gross sales revenue.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(b)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>The impairment charges of US$982&nbsp;million for the year ended 31 December&nbsp;2010 related
mainly to Alcan Engineered Products businesses: US$805&nbsp;million, the Group&#146;s diamond
businesses: US$135&nbsp;million (net of impairment reversals) and US$42&nbsp;million in other
impairments.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>The impairment charges of US$1,573&nbsp;million for the year ended 31 December&nbsp;2009 related
mainly to a write-down on Alcan Engineered Products of US$687&nbsp;million, the Group&#146;s aluminium
businesses of US$304&nbsp;million, US$525&nbsp;million on the Group&#146;s diamond businesses and US$57&nbsp;million
in other impairments.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>All impairments were measured based upon an assessment of fair value. Alcan
Packaging is discussed separately in (e)&nbsp;below.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(c)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto consolidated Oyu Tolgoi LLC on 15 December&nbsp;2010 following the signing of a new
agreement with Ivanhoe Mines. A gain of US$531&nbsp;million arose on consolidation, representing the
excess of the provisional fair value ascribed to the Group&#146;s indirect share of the assets and
liabilities of Oyu Tolgoi LLC over the historic cost of acquiring that share through its
investment in Ivanhoe Mines Ltd. Refer to acquisitions and disposals on page 37.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Profits arising on the disposal of interests in businesses for the year ended 31 December
2010 relate principally to sale of the Group&#146;s 48 per cent interest in Cloud Peak Energy Inc.
Refer to acquisitions and disposals on page 37.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Profits arising on the disposal of interests in businesses in 2009 related principally
to sales of the Corumb&#225; iron ore mine, the Jacobs Ranch coal mine, the sale of 52 per cent of
Rio Tinto&#146;s interest in Cloud Peak Energy Resources LLC (CPER)&nbsp;and are partially offset by a
loss from the sale of Alcan Composites.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(d)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Profits on disposal of interests in undeveloped projects in 2010 relate principally to
the disposal of undeveloped coal projects at Vickery and Maules Creek. The 2009 profits
relate principally to the disposal of undeveloped potash assets in Argentina and Canada.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(e)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Loss after tax from discontinued operations of US$97&nbsp;million relates to the completion of
the disposal of Alcan Packaging global pharmaceuticals, global tobacco, food Europe and food
Asia divisions to Amcor on 1 February&nbsp;2010, and Alcan Food Packaging Americas division to
Bemis Company Inc. on 1 March&nbsp;2010.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>An impairment of US$318&nbsp;million was recognised at 31 December&nbsp;2009, relating to the Alcan
Packaging business and was included in &#145;Loss after tax from discontinued operations&#146;. This
impairment was based on an estimate of fair value less costs to sell. Additionally, &#145;Loss after
tax from discontinued operations&#146; included a US$131&nbsp;million tax charge for 31 December&nbsp;2009
relating to an increase in the Group&#146;s estimate of the tax to be paid on sale of the Alcan
Packaging business. This increase in estimate followed a detailed review of the changes to the
proposed sale structure.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(f)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>For the purposes of calculating basic earnings/(loss) per share, the weighted average
number of Rio Tinto plc and Rio Tinto Limited shares outstanding during the year was 1,961.0
million (31 December&nbsp;2009: 1,763.6&nbsp;million), being the weighted average number of Rio Tinto plc
shares outstanding of 1,525.2&nbsp;million (31 December&nbsp;2009: 1,366.1&nbsp;million), plus the weighted
average number of Rio Tinto Limited shares outstanding not held by Rio Tinto plc of 435.8
million (31 December&nbsp;2009: 397.5&nbsp;million). The profit figure used in the calculation of basic
and diluted earnings per share is based on profit for the year attributable to equity
shareholders of Rio Tinto.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>For the purposes of calculating diluted earnings per share, the effect of dilutive
securities is added to the weighted average number of shares. This effect is calculated using
the treasury stock method.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>The 2009 rights issues were at a discount to the then market price. Accordingly, both
earnings and dividends per share for all periods up to the date on which the shares were issued
in July&nbsp;2009 have been adjusted for the bonus element of the issues. The bonus factor for Rio
Tinto plc was 1.2105 and for Rio Tinto Limited was 1.2679.</TD>
</TR>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Notes
to the Group statement of financial position</B>
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(a)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>At 31 December&nbsp;2010 assets and liabilities held for sale comprise Alcan&#146;s Engineered
Products group (AEP)&nbsp;excluding the Cable Division. The classification of Engineered Products
follows the announcement of the receipt of a binding offer on 5 August&nbsp;2010. The sale of 61 per
cent of AEP excluding the Cable Division, was completed on 4 January&nbsp;2011. After the
transaction, Rio Tinto holds a 39 per cent stake, which is treated as an equity accounted unit.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Assets and liabilities held for sale as at 31 December&nbsp;2009 primarily comprise the Alcan
Packaging group, which was acquired with a view to resale, and other assets held for sale.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" nowrap align="left">(b)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>At 31 December&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto plc had 1,526.3&nbsp;million ordinary shares in issue and held by
the public, and Rio Tinto Limited had 435.8&nbsp;million shares in issue. No shares in Rio Tinto
Limited were held by Rio Tinto plc at 31 December&nbsp;2010 (31 December&nbsp;2009: US$171.1&nbsp;million). As
required to be disclosed under the ASX Listing Rules, the net tangible assets per share amounted
to US$19.03 (31 December&nbsp;2009: US$12.16).</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Reconciliation with Australian Accounting Standards</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Group&#146;s financial statements have been prepared in accordance with IFRS as adopted by
the European Union (&#145;EU IFRS&#146;), which differs in certain respects from the version of IFRS that
is applicable in Australia, referred to as Australian Accounting Standards (AAS).
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Prior to 1 January&nbsp;2004, the Group&#146;s financial statements were prepared in accordance with UK
GAAP. Under EU IFRS goodwill on acquisitions prior to 1998, which was eliminated directly
against equity in the Group&#146;s UK GAAP financial statements, has not been reinstated. This was
permitted under the rules governing the transition to EU IFRS set out in IFRS 1. The equivalent
Australian Standard, AASB 1, does not provide for the netting of goodwill against equity. As a
consequence, shareholders&#146; funds under AAS include the residue of such goodwill, which amounted
to US$584&nbsp;million at 31 December&nbsp;2010 (2009: US$597&nbsp;million).
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Save for the exception described above, the Group&#146;s financial statements drawn up in
accordance with EU IFRS are consistent with the requirements of AAS.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#145;Underlying earnings&#146; is an alternative measure of earnings, which is reported by Rio
Tinto to provide greater understanding of the underlying business performance of its
operations. Underlying earnings and Net earnings both represent amounts attributable to Rio
Tinto shareholders. Items (a)&nbsp;to (h)&nbsp;below are excluded from Net earnings in arriving at
Underlying earnings.
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">(a)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto consolidated Oyu Tolgoi LLC on 15 December&nbsp;2010 following the signing of a new
agreement with Ivanhoe Mines. The gain arising on consolidation represents the excess of the
provisional fair value ascribed to the Group&#146;s indirect share of the assets and liabilities of
Oyu Tolgoi over the historic cost of acquiring that share through its investment in Ivanhoe
Mines Ltd.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left">(b)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Profits arising on the disposal of interests in businesses for the year ended 31 December
2010 relate principally to the sale of the Group&#146;s 48 per cent interest in Cloud Peak Energy
Inc. Refer to acquisitions and disposals on page 37.</TD>
</TR>

    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Acquisitions and Disposals</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>2010 Acquisitions</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><I>Consolidation of Oyu Tolgoi LLC</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 15 December&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto gained control of Oyu Tolgoi LLC, following the signing of a
new agreement with Ivanhoe Mines Ltd (&#145;Ivanhoe&#146;). Oyu Tolgoi LLC is consolidated by virtue of
Rio Tinto&#146;s contractual rights which permit it to exercise control over certain policies and
activities of Oyu Tolgoi LLC. No direct equity interest was acquired under the agreement and
the existing equity arrangements were not changed as a result of the agreement. Oyu Tolgoi LLC
is owned 66 per cent by Ivanhoe and 34 per cent by the Government of Mongolia. The signing of
the agreement did not affect the Government of Mongolia&#146;s economic interest in Oyu Tolgoi LLC.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">As part of the agreement by which Rio Tinto obtained its contractual rights, Rio Tinto agreed to
exercise its remaining warrants for common shares in Ivanhoe, participate fully in Ivanhoe&#146;s
US$1.2&nbsp;billion rights offering, and to provide Ivanhoe with a US$1.8&nbsp;billion interim loan
facility to fund the Oyu Tolgoi project.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The agreement secured for Rio Tinto the right to increase its ownership in Ivanhoe to 49 per
cent by, in addition to exercising its remaining warrants for common shares, acquiring a total
of twenty million shares at current market prices, evenly from Citibank and Ivanhoe executive
chairman and chief executive officer, Robert Friedland, purchasing shares in the market, and
exercising its right to subscribe for Ivanhoe common shares from treasury at market prices
until January&nbsp;2012.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 15 December&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto exercised 33,783,784 Series&nbsp;B warrants for common shares at an
exercise price of US$8.88 per share, paying a total of US$300&nbsp;million, and acquired ten million
shares in Ivanhoe from Robert Friedland at a market price of US$25.34 per share, paying a total
of US$253&nbsp;million. These transactions increased Rio Tinto&#146;s ownership in Ivanhoe to 40.5 per
cent.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Acquisitions and Disposals (continued)</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">100 per cent of Oyu Tolgoi LLC&#146;s identifiable assets and liabilities have been recognised in the
statement of financial position at fair values estimated with the assistance of an independent
third party valuer, together with goodwill. The historic cost of acquiring the Group&#146;s indirect
share of Oyu Tolgoi LLC through its investment in Ivanhoe was deducted from investments in
Equity Accounted Units. The Group&#146;s remaining interest in the assets of Ivanhoe that does not
relate to Oyu Tolgoi LLC continues to be equity accounted. The transaction generated a non cash
gain of US$531&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Due to the complexity of the valuation process, and the proximity of the date on which the
agreement was effective to the reporting date, fair values on consolidation are provisional and
will be subject to further review during the 12&nbsp;months from the date on which the agreement was
effective.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Oyu Tolgoi LLC owns and manages the Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold complex in Mongolia, where full
scale mine construction and development of a copper concentrator and related infrastructure
are underway.
</DIV>

provisionally estimated as follows:
