<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Acquisitions and Disposals (continued)</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Had Oyu Tolgoi been consolidated from 1 January&nbsp;2010, the consolidated income statement would
have reduced by US$118&nbsp;million to show profit after tax (before attributing amounts to
non-controlling interests) of US$15,066&nbsp;million. Consolidated sales revenue would have been
unaffected.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Ivanhoe Mines Limited</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In addition to the agreement described above, during the year ended 31 December&nbsp;2010 Rio Tinto
also entered into the transactions described below in relation to its investment in Ivanhoe
Mines Limited (&#145;Ivanhoe&#146;).
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 1 March&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto announced that it had agreed to acquire 15&nbsp;million shares in Ivanhoe
at a subscription price of C$16.31 per share, increasing its ownership in Ivanhoe by 2.7 per
cent to 22.4 per cent. The total consideration for this acquisition was C$244.7&nbsp;million (US$241
million). The shares were issued to Rio Tinto in satisfaction of an agreement with Ivanhoe in
2008 to finance equipment for the Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold complex in Mongolia&#146;s South Gobi
region. After the completion of the acquisition, Rio Tinto owned 98.6&nbsp;million shares in Ivanhoe.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 30 June&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto increased its ownership in Ivanhoe to 29.6 per cent following the
exercising of all its Series&nbsp;A warrants for a total consideration of US$393&nbsp;million. After the
completion of the exercise of the Series&nbsp;A warrants, Rio Tinto owned 144.66&nbsp;million shares in
Ivanhoe.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 13 September&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto increased its ownership to 34.9 per cent following automatic
conversion of the US$350&nbsp;million convertible debt facility Rio Tinto made available to Ivanhoe
in 2007, which was fully drawn down by mid 2008. After the completion of the conversion of the
debt facility, Rio Tinto owned 184.75&nbsp;million shares in Ivanhoe.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">There were no other significant acquisitions for the year ended 31 December&nbsp;2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>2009 Acquisitions</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 28 October&nbsp;2009, Rio Tinto completed the second tranche of its private placement investment
in Ivanhoe Mines Ltd, increasing its ownership by 9.8 per cent to 19.7 per cent of Ivanhoe&#146;s
common shares. The second tranche consists of 46,304,473 common shares at a subscription price
of US$8.38 per share for a total consideration of US$388&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">There were no other significant acquisitions for the year ended 31 December&nbsp;2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>2010 Disposals</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto completed the sale of Alcan Packaging global pharmaceuticals, global tobacco, food
Europe and food Asia divisions to Amcor for a total consideration of US$1,948&nbsp;million on 1
February&nbsp;2010. The consideration was adjusted to exclude Medical Flexibles operations and to
reflect actual business performance over the six months preceding completion.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s 75.7 per cent owned subsidiary Coal &#038; Allied sold the Maules Creek project to Aston
Resources, a private Australian company, for A$480&nbsp;million (US$427&nbsp;million). The sale was
completed on 18 February&nbsp;2010. Coal &#038; Allied&#146;s Vickery asset was sold to Whitehaven Coal (ASX
listed) for A$31.5&nbsp;million (US$28&nbsp;million), with an effective date of 4 February&nbsp;2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The sale of the Alcan Packaging Food Americas division to Bemis Company Inc., for a total
consideration of US$1.2&nbsp;billion was completed on 1 March&nbsp;2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 5 July&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto completed the divestment of the remainder of its Alcan Packaging
business with the closing of the sale of the Medical Flexibles business acquired by Amcor for
US$66&nbsp;million and of the sale of the Alcan Beauty Packaging business acquired by Sun European
Partners LLP for an undisclosed sum.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Acquisitions and Disposals (continued)</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 5 August&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto received a binding offer from funds affiliated with Apollo
Global Management, L.P. (Apollo) and the Fonds Strat&#233;gique d&#146;Investissement (FSI)&nbsp;to buy a 61
per cent stake in Alcan Engineered Products (AEP), excluding the Cable Division. The divestment
was completed on 4 January&nbsp;2011. The terms of the transaction are confidential. Refer to Events
after the statement of financial position date on page 41.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 21 December&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto completed the divestment of its remaining 48 per cent
interest in Cloud Peak Energy Inc., through a secondary offering, for gross proceeds of
US$573&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Proposed Simandou transaction with Chalco</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 29 July&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto and Chalco signed a binding agreement to establish a joint venture
(JV)&nbsp;covering the development and operation of the Simandou iron ore project in Guinea. The
binding agreement followed the signing of a memorandum of understanding between Rio Tinto and
Chalco&#146;s parent Chinalco announced on 19 March&nbsp;2010. The agreement covers all aspects of how the
JV and the project itself will operate and be governed, including planning, construction and
management of the mine and associated rail and port infrastructure. Under the terms of the
agreement, Rio Tinto&#146;s 95 per cent interest in the Simandou project will be held in the new JV.
Chalco will acquire a 47 per cent interest in the new JV by providing US$1.35&nbsp;billion on an
earn-in basis through sole funding of ongoing development work over the next two to three years.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Once Chalco has paid its US$1.35&nbsp;billion, the effective interests of Rio Tinto and Chalco in the
Simandou project would be 50.35 per cent and 44.65 per cent respectively. The remaining five per
cent is owned by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the financing arm of the World
Bank. Rio Tinto will retain control of the entity established to own the project.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Government of Guinea holds an option to acquire up to a 20% interest in the project, and
has indicated an intention to exercise this option. Upon the exercise taking effect, the
effective interests in the project of each of Rio Tinto, Chalco and IFC would be reduced
proportionately; however control would be retained by Rio Tinto.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The formation of the Rio Tinto/Chalco JV remains subject to the satisfaction of certain
regulatory requirements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Once the JV takes effect, a wholly owned subsidiary of Rio Tinto will be appointed manager of
the project, providing management services to the JV and being responsible for the day-to-day
operations of the project. Rio Tinto and Chalco will also establish a joint marketing company to
market and distribute Simandou product to customers under an agency agreement with a wholly
owned subsidiary of Rio Tinto.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Chinalco and Rio Tinto have entered into an agreement under which Chinalco guarantees the
performance of Chalco&#146;s obligations under the Agreement.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto will continue to account for its interest in the Simandou project as a subsidiary.
The contributions to funding made by Chalco to acquire an interest in the project will be
credited to equity.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>2009 Disposals</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 1 December&nbsp;2009, Rio Tinto completed the sale of Alcan Composites, part of Alcan
Engineered Products, to Schweiter Technologies for a total consideration of US$349&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 20 November&nbsp;2009, Rio Tinto received US$741&nbsp;million in connection with Cloud Peak Energy
Inc&#146;s initial public offering (IPO)&nbsp;and related transactions, comprising US$434&nbsp;million net
proceeds from the sale of part of Rio Tinto&#146;s interest in Cloud Peak Energy Resources LLC
(CPER), in connection with Cloud Peak Energy Inc&#146;s IPO of common stock, and a cash distribution
by CPER of US$307&nbsp;million from the proceeds of its debt offering of US$600&nbsp;million. An
additional US$7&nbsp;million was received as part of a working capital adjustment at 31 December
2009. Rio Tinto retained an interest in CPER of 48 per cent, which was treated as an equity
accounted unit (EAU)&nbsp;until its disposal on 21 December&nbsp;2010.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Acquisitions and Disposals (continued)</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">US$660&nbsp;million of sales proceeds arose from these transactions and US$151&nbsp;million was received
as dividends from an EAU. The sales proceeds comprised the gross IPO proceeds of US$459&nbsp;million,
52 per cent of the cash distribution by CPER (representing the percentage not retained by the
Group) and US$38&nbsp;million of deferred consideration.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 1 October&nbsp;2009, Rio Tinto completed the sale of its Jacobs Ranch coal mine to Arch Coal
Inc. for a final cash consideration of US$764&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 18 September&nbsp;2009, Rio Tinto completed the sale of its Corumb&#225; iron ore mine and
associated river logistics operations to Vale SA for a cash consideration of US$750&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 26 January&nbsp;2009, Rio Tinto completed the sale of its 50&nbsp;percent equity share of the Alcan
Ningxia aluminium joint venture in China to Qingtongxia Aluminium Group Co Ltd (QTX)&nbsp;for gross
cash consideration of US$125&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Rights issues</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The terms of the rights issues in 2009 were; 21 New Rio Tinto plc Shares offered for every
40 existing shares at 1,400 pence per share and 21 New Rio Tinto Limited Shares offered for
every 40 existing shares at A$28.29 per share and were completed on 2 July&nbsp;2009 and 3 July&nbsp;2009
respectively.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Both Rio Tinto plc and Rio Tinto Limited entered into a series of forward US dollar derivative
exchange contracts to minimise exposure to foreign exchange rates and provide confidence in
absolute US dollar rights issue proceeds. The forward contracts taken out by both companies were
accounted for as derivatives, for which different accounting treatments were applied in
accordance with IFRS hedge accounting rules. This was due to the different functional currencies
of Rio Tinto plc and Rio Tinto Limited (US dollar and Australian dollar respectively). Losses on
contracts entered into by Rio Tinto plc were charged against share premium as share issue costs
while losses on the contracts entered into by Rio Tinto Limited were recognised in the income
statement and excluded from Underlying earnings. Settlement of losses on all contracts were
included within &#145;Other investing cash flows&#146; in the statement of cash flow.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Events after the statement of financial position date</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 4 January&nbsp;2011, Rio Tinto completed the divestment of 61 per cent of Alcan Engineered
Products (AEP)&nbsp;to certain investment funds affiliated with Apollo Global Management, LLC
(Apollo) and the Fonds Strat&#233;gique d&#146;Investissement (FSI). The terms of the transaction are
confidential.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Apollo is now the majority shareholder in AEP with a 51 per cent stake in a new holding
company for AEP, with the FSI holding 10 per cent. Rio Tinto holds a 39 per cent stake and
will treat its interest in AEP as an equity accounted unit.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 3 February, Rio Tinto acquired an additional 34,387,776 additional shares in Ivanhoe Mines
Ltd (&#145;Ivanhoe&#146;), by participating fully in Ivanhoe&#146;s strategic rights offering, paying a total
of US$477&nbsp;million and maintaining the Group&#146;s interest in Ivanhoe. On 3rd February, Rio Tinto
also completed the purchase of ten million shares in Ivanhoe, together with the rights (1.5
million shares) associated with these shares from Citibank, in accordance with the announcement
made on 15 December&nbsp;2010, paying a total of US$274&nbsp;million. The transaction increased Rio
Tinto&#146;s ownership of Ivanhoe to 42.1 per cent.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Accounting policies</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The financial information included in this report has been prepared on the basis of all
IFRSs and Interpretations adopted by the European Union that are mandatory for periods ending 31
December&nbsp;2010 and in accordance with: applicable United Kingdom law, applicable Australian law
as amended by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission Order dated 22 December&nbsp;2010;
and Article&nbsp;4 of the European Union IAS regulation.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The EU IFRS financial information has been drawn up on the basis of accounting policies
consistent with those applied in the financial statements for the year to 31 December&nbsp;2009,
except for IFRS 3 (revised) &#145;Business combinations&#146;, amendments to IAS 27 (revised)
&#145;Consolidated and separate financial statements&#146; and those Improvements to IFRS 2009 which are
mandatory for 2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The effect of adopting these standards, where the standards require retrospective application,
is not material to Group earnings or to shareholders&#146; funds in the prior year. Therefore, prior
year information has not been restated. A post tax gain of US$531m has been recorded on the
control of Oyu Tolgoi LLC in 2010 as a result of the application of the amendment to IFRS 3 with
a consequent increase in the provisional fair value of identifiable net assets associated with
the transaction.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Certain of the Group&#146;s products, such as iron ore, were previously sold under long term
contracts at a benchmark price. During 2010 pricing for the majority of iron ore customers
changed to a quarterly basis reflecting the structural shift away from annual benchmark
pricing. Consistent with prior years, where the benchmark price has not been formally agreed
by individual customers at the end of an accounting period, revenue is reported based on the
best available information, having reference to the terms of the contractual agreement and,
where appropriate, to sales with other customers.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Status of financial information</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">This preliminary announcement does not constitute the Group&#146;s full financial statements
for 2010. This report is based on accounts which are in the process of being audited and will
be approved by the Board and subsequently filed with the Registrar of Companies and the
Australian Securities and Investments Commission. Accordingly, the financial information for
2010 is unaudited and does not have the status of statutory accounts within the meaning of
Section&nbsp;434 of the Companies Act 2006.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Financial information for the year to 31 December&nbsp;2009 has been extracted from the full
financial statements prepared under the historical cost convention, as modified by the
revaluation of certain derivative contracts, financial assets and post-retirement assets and
liabilities, as filed with the Registrar of Companies. The Auditors&#146; report on the full
financial statements for the year to 31 December&nbsp;2009 was unqualified and did not contain
statements under section 237(2) of the United Kingdom Companies Act 1985 (regarding adequacy
of accounting records and returns), or under 237(3) (regarding provision of necessary
information and explanations).
</DIV>

</DIV>
